submissions.title: Meta Announces New Strategic Venture with BlackRock to Develop Data Center in El Paso
submissions.excerpt: BlackRock funds will own about 80% of the venture, delivering 1 gigawatt of compute capacity for Meta
submissions.suggestedProjectName: Meta El Paso Data Center (BlackRock JV)
submissions.note: New $14B JV (BlackRock funds ~80%, Meta ~20%) to develop/own an existing under-construction El Paso, TX campus; Meta contributes ~$2.3B in land/partially-built assets, BlackRock ~$4.9B cash. 1 GW is stated IT/compute capacity (not site power draw), completion targeted 2028, Meta sole occupant. This is an ownership/financing restructuring of a campus that may already be tracked under Meta's name in El Paso -- check for an existing project before creating a new one. submissions.title: Core Scientific Doubles AI Capacity to 1.1 GW in $14B AMD Deal
submissions.excerpt: 15-year infrastructure agreement with AMD covering 530 MW across five campuses
submissions.suggestedProjectName: Core Scientific AI Campuses (AMD deal, 530 MW / 5 sites)
submissions.note: Core Scientific signed a 15-year deal with AMD across five campuses, doubling its leased AI capacity to ~1.1 GW total; AMD also holds an option to reserve up to 2 GW more (a reservation right, not a firm commitment). IMPORTANT: the widely-reported '$14B' figure is base contracted lease revenue over 15 years, NOT capex -- per tracker policy this is deliberately not submitted as a CAPEX_USD claim. 530 MW is the disclosed IT power commitment for this deal. Likely a new entry for the tracker (Core Scientific is pivoting from bitcoin mining to AI hosting) -- verify it isn't already tracked under a different framing (e.g. as bitcoin-mining-to-AI conversion capacity).

claims.methodology: Capacity commitment across 5 campuses per company deal disclosure, as covered in press

submissions.title: Council Approves 18-Month Data Center Moratorium and Places Limitations on Data Center Development
submissions.excerpt: block any data centers larger than 25 megawatts from being built in the county
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Montgomery County Council (MD) unanimously passed Expedited Bill 19-26 on 2026-07-28 (lead sponsor Evan Glass): an 18-month moratorium barring the Dept. of Permitting Services from issuing data-center permits, plus a zoning-text amendment defining/capping non-conforming data centers at 25 MW aggregate monthly electricity demand. It was a compromise between a 6-month moratorium (Glass) and a 2-year pause (Jawando/Mink). This is a jurisdiction-wide restriction, not linked to a specific tracked project -- a reviewer should attach it to any tracked/prospective projects sited in Montgomery County, MD. Caveat: WebFetch to the county's own press release returned an error this session (tool outage); excerpt reconstructed from corroborating coverage (Food & Water Watch, The Banner, WTOP) -- verify wording against the primary link before promoting.

claims.methodology: Zoning threshold (aggregate monthly electricity demand) defining a regulated data center, per the approved ordinance as reported

submissions.title: La Conner Town Council approves temporary moratorium on data centers
submissions.excerpt: placed a temporary moratorium on accepting data center permit applications ... in effect for at least six months
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: La Conner, WA (small town, Skagit County) Town Council adopted a preemptive 6-month moratorium on data center permit applications -- no project is currently proposed or pending; the stated concern is proximity to a large water source data centers would depend on. Mirrors Skagit County's unincorporated-area moratorium adopted 2026-06-01. Low individual materiality but part of a growing WA state cluster (Pasco, Seattle, Skagit County) worth tracking as a pattern of preemptive local bans even absent a filed project.

submissions.title: Pallone Demands Answers from SpaceX/xAI About Its Data Center Threats to Tennessee & Mississippi Communities
submissions.publisher: House Committee on Energy and Commerce, Democrats (Rep. Frank Pallone)
submissions.excerpt: demanding a tour of his company's xAI data centers and power plants in and around Memphis
submissions.note: Congressional oversight letter from House E&C ranking member Pallone to Elon Musk (SpaceX/xAI), sent 2026-07-29, demanding a facility tour, a full inventory of gas turbines powering Colossus 1 (Shelby County, TN) and Colossus 2 (DeSoto County/Southaven, MS), emissions and permitting records, and communications with state/local/federal officials -- citing unpermitted turbine fleets and Clean Air Act concerns at both sites. This is a regulatory-risk status update on a project very likely already tracked (xAI Colossus), not a change to any MW/capex figure -- flag for reviewer attention rather than a claims update. No numeric claims submitted here since the letter's content is a request for information, not a disclosed figure.
